sections.skill: Judge whether evidence supports a claim: samples, comparisons and correlation

questions.prompt: To learn how often people in a town exercise, a student surveys 100 people leaving a gym. What is the main problem with this evidence?

choices.text: People leaving a gym probably exercise more than the town as a whole.
The survey should have asked about diet too.
100 people is always too few for a survey.
Surveys can never give useful evidence.

questions.correct_answer: People leaving a gym probably exercise more than the town as a whole.

questions.prompt: School A: 45 of its 60 students passed a test. School B: 52 of its 80 students passed. What percent of School A's students passed?
In many towns, more ice-cream sales come with more swimming accidents. This shows that eating ice cream causes swimming accidents.

choices.text: True
False

questions.prompt: Which study design gives the best evidence that a tutoring program raises test scores?

choices.text: Measure the scores of tutored students only.
Compare tutored students with students who chose not to sign up.
Randomly assign students to get tutoring or not, then compare the two groups' scores.
Ask tutored students whether they feel they improved.

questions.correct_answer: Randomly assign students to get tutoring or not, then compare the two groups' scores.

questions.prompt: A claim says that more than half of a school's students prefer a later start time. In a random sample of 40 students, n said they prefer it. Give a value of n that would support the claim.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n > 20 and n <= 40 (example: n = 28)

sections.relationship: Most evidence questions compare groups of different sizes. Students who compare raw counts instead of rates draw the wrong conclusion.
sections.author_note: Most evidence questions compare groups of different sizes. Students who compare raw counts instead of rates draw the wrong conclusion.

questions.prompt: 18 of 24 students in a class walk to school. What percent is that?
Club X has 30 members and 12 play chess. Club Y has 10 members and 6 play chess. A larger share of Club Y plays chess.

choices.text: True
False

questions.prompt: Town P had 50 car accidents and Town Q had 30. What else do you need before saying Town P's roads are more dangerous?

choices.text: The colors of the cars
Nothing; 50 is more than 30
The names of the drivers
How many people or cars each town has

questions.correct_answer: How many people or cars each town has

questions.prompt: A survey of 200 people finds that 30 own a bike. What percent own a bike?
If Group A has more members with a trait than Group B, then a larger percent of Group A has the trait.

choices.text: True
False

questions.prompt: A website asks visitors to vote on whether the town needs a new park. Of 300 votes, 80% say yes. Why is this weak evidence about the whole town?

choices.text: 80% is too high to be believed.
300 votes is more than enough.
Websites cannot count votes.
People who choose to vote online may care more about parks than others.

questions.correct_answer: People who choose to vote online may care more about parks than others.

questions.prompt: Class A: 21 of 28 students finished the project on time. Class B: 24 of 30. What is the higher of the two on-time percents?
A study finds that students who own more books tend to have higher reading scores. This alone proves that buying books raises reading scores.

choices.text: True
False

questions.prompt: To test whether a new fertilizer helps tomato plants grow, which design is best?

choices.text: Give fertilizer to a randomly chosen half of the plants and compare them with the other half.
Give fertilizer to all plants and measure them.
Ask a gardener whether the plants look bigger.
Use the fertilizer only on the healthiest plants.

questions.correct_answer: Give fertilizer to a randomly chosen half of the plants and compare them with the other half.

questions.prompt: A coin is flipped 50 times to test whether it is fair. Give a number of heads h from 0 to 50 that would be strong evidence the coin favors heads. Use this test: h is at least 35.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(h) and h >= 35 and h <= 50 (example: h = 40)

sections.relationship: Expert: combined groups and base rates.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: Two clinics treat a condition. Clinic A treats 100 mild cases (90 recover) and 20 severe cases (8 recover). Clinic B treats 20 mild cases (19 recover) and 100 severe cases (50 recover). What percent of all Clinic A patients recover, to the nearest whole percent?

Two clinics treat a condition. Clinic A: 100 mild cases (90 recover) and 20 severe cases (8 recover). Clinic B: 20 mild cases (19 recover) and 100 severe cases (50 recover). Overall, Clinic A has the higher recovery rate (about 82% to 58%). Which statement is true?

choices.text: Clinic A is better for both mild and severe cases.
Clinic B has the higher recovery rate for mild cases AND for severe cases.
Clinic A must be the better clinic.
The two clinics are equally good for mild cases.

questions.correct_answer: Clinic B has the higher recovery rate for mild cases AND for severe cases.

questions.prompt: Two clinics treat a condition. Clinic A: 100 mild cases (90 recover) and 20 severe cases (8 recover). Clinic B: 20 mild cases (19 recover) and 100 severe cases (50 recover). Comparing only the overall recovery rates gives a fair comparison of the clinics.

choices.text: True
False

questions.prompt: A test for a rare condition is positive for 95 of every 100 people who have it and for 5 of every 100 people who do not. In a town of 10,000 people, 100 have the condition. About how many people in the town test positive in all?
Of 590 people who test positive for a condition, 95 actually have it. What fraction of the positive tests are correct?

choices.text: About 5%
About 50%
About 16%
About 95%
